items.q: In the 'Dependent on' list, the page prints the sex line as 'Sex (↓ in males)'.
opts: True — the printed wording is ↓ in males
False — the page reads ↓ in females
True — and race carries the identical downward arrow for males
False — sex is not one of the listed determinants
items.exp: The four bullets are muscle mass (↓ muscle mass → ↓ Cr), race (↓ in African Americans), age (↓ after 40 years d/t ↓ in muscle mass) and sex (↓ in males) — quote the page wording, even though greater muscle mass usually makes male creatinine higher. (Book p736)

items.q: Six hours after a crush injury the serum creatinine is still 0.9 mg/dL although urine output has fallen. Which line on this page accounts for that?
opts: Creatinine takes 24–48 hrs to start rising in AKI
Creatinine is reabsorbed by the tubule in injury
Muscle mass drops instantly, normalising the value
Trauma increases tubular secretion of creatinine
items.exp: Disadvantage 1 reads: 24–48 hrs to start rising in Acute Kidney Injury (AKI) — an early normal creatinine does not exclude AKI. (Book p736)

items.q: Cimetidine and trimethoprim raise the serum creatinine through every step of the printed flowchart EXCEPT:
opts: Increased tubular secretion of creatinine
Competition with creatinine for tubular secretion
Reduced tubular secretion of creatinine
A rise in serum creatinine
items.exp: The flow reads: compete with Cr for tubular secretion → ↓ tubular secretion of Cr → ↑ serum Cr; secretion falls rather than rises. (Book p736)

items.q: A dialysis-dependent patient's creatinine rises from 5 to 20 mg/dL over a month. Per the page's reading of the inverse curve:
opts: The fall in GFR is insignificant — the patient was already in ESRD
GFR has fallen from 50 to 30 ml/min
GFR has halved from 60 to 30 ml/min
GFR is unchanged, because the curve is linear in this range
items.exp: Worked example: ↑ S.Cr from 5 to 20 → fall in GFR is insignificant (patient was already in ESRD), whereas 1.7 → 2.8 marks 50 → 30 ml/min. (Book p736)

items.q: The page states that a rise in serum creatinine from 1.7 to 2.8 mg/dL corresponds to a fall in GFR from about 50 to about 30 ml/min.
opts: True — this is the second worked example under the curve
False — this rise is described as insignificant
True — and the same is said for a rise from 5 to 20 mg/dL
False — the pair quoted for this range is 125 to 100 ml/min
items.exp: Both examples sit under the graph: S.Cr 1.7 → 2.8 gives GFR 50 → 30 ml/min (significant fall), while 5 → 20 is insignificant in established ESRD. (Book p736)

items.q: Fill up: Reduced protein supplementation and malnutrition both lower serum creatinine by decreasing ______.
opts: Muscle mass
Glomerular filtration
Tubular secretion
Plasma volume
items.exp: Diet alters S.Cr: ↓ protein supplementation → ↓ muscle mass → ↓ S.Cr, and malnutrition → ↓ muscle mass → ↓ S.Cr. (Book p736)

items.q: Serum creatinine declines with age after which point, because muscle mass falls?
opts: After 40 years
After 20 years
After 60 years
After 30 years
items.exp: Dependent on: Age (↓ after 40 years d/t ↓ in muscle mass). (Book p736)
